headline: Tk 20 hike: Jamaat urges govt to withdraw fuel price increase
summary: Secretary General Mia Golam Porwar warns that the hike will put additional economic pressure on low- and middle-income people and drive up essential commodity prices.
details: Jamaat-e-Islami Secretary General Mia Golam Porwar has criticised the government's decision to increase fuel prices by Tk 20 per litre, calling for an immediate withdrawal of the move.
Porwar stated that the purchasing power of low- and middle-income citizens has already been severely affected by rising commodity prices, and this hike adds further burden.
He warned that the impact would extend beyond vehicle users, as fuel is a critical component of transportation and production across various sectors.
According to the party leader, higher fuel costs will increase agricultural, transport, and industrial production costs, eventually pushing up the prices of essential goods.
Porwar argued that the government should have considered the overall economic situation and people's income levels before implementing the price hike.
He suggested alternative measures such as cutting unnecessary government expenditure, preventing waste, and improving fuel management to avoid passing international market volatility onto the public.
The Secretary General also called for stronger market monitoring to contain commodity prices and prevent irregularities by middlemen.
caption:
Fuel prices jump by Tk 20 per litre. Jamaat-e-Islami warns of a fresh economic crisis for ordinary citizens.

Jamaat-e-Islami Secretary General Mia Golam Porwar has criticised the government's decision to increase fuel prices by Tk 20 per litre, calling for an immediate withdrawal of the move.

Porwar stated that the purchasing power of low- and middle-income citizens has already been severely affected by rising commodity prices, and this hike adds further burden.

He warned that the impact would extend beyond vehicle users, as fuel is a critical component of transportation and production across various sectors.

According to the party leader, higher fuel costs will increase agricultural, transport, and industrial production costs, eventually pushing up the prices of essential goods.

Porwar argued that the government should have considered the overall economic situation and people's income levels before implementing the price hike.

He suggested alternative measures such as cutting unnecessary government expenditure, preventing waste, and improving fuel management to avoid passing international market volatility onto the public.

The Secretary General also called for stronger market monitoring to contain commodity prices and prevent irregularities by middlemen.

Source: Prothom Alo, The Daily Star, Dhaka Tribune

headline: MP Gazi Nazrul placed on 4-day remand over second wife's death
summary: The lawmaker and his first wife were arrested for allegedly abetting the suicide of Mariam Khatun, whose body was found in a Dhaka flat.
details: A Dhaka court has placed Satkhira-4 MP Gazi Nazrul Islam and his first wife, Maksuda Begum, on remand in connection with the death of his second wife, Mariam Khatun.
The lawmaker was placed on a four-day remand, while his first wife was placed on a one-day remand.
The case was filed by the victim's father, SM Masum Billah, at Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station under Section 306 of the Penal Code for abetment of suicide.
Mariam Khatun's body was recovered from a flat at NAM Bhaban in Dhaka yesterday afternoon.
Prior to the arrest, MP Gazi Nazrul had submitted a bail bond in an unrelated attempted murder case filed in July by his former driver.
The Election Commission has stated that the lawmaker's parliamentary status will be decided by the Speaker of the Parliament and the EC.
caption:
An MP and his first wife are in police custody. They are accused of abetting the suicide of the lawmaker's second wife.

A Dhaka court has placed Satkhira-4 MP Gazi Nazrul Islam and his first wife, Maksuda Begum, on remand in connection with the death of his second wife, Mariam Khatun.

The lawmaker was placed on a four-day remand, while his first wife was placed on a one-day remand.

The case was filed by the victim's father, SM Masum Billah, at Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station under Section 306 of the Penal Code for abetment of suicide.

Mariam Khatun's body was recovered from a flat at NAM Bhaban in Dhaka yesterday afternoon.

Prior to the arrest, MP Gazi Nazrul had submitted a bail bond in an unrelated attempted murder case filed in July by his former driver.

The Election Commission has stated that the lawmaker's parliamentary status will be decided by the Speaker of the Parliament and the EC.
